turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Hale. I'm Meredith Kalinowski, Owen's mother. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's begin.

You gave my son a zero, and I found out because he saw it on his phone in the middle of your class. Why?
I came because nobody called me first. The zero went into the gradebook, and my son read it on his phone in front of his class. I'm waiting for your reason, Hale.
How do I wrap up this meeting?
You answer my question, and then I leave. Why did you enter that zero before calling me?
What happens after we finish? Do I get a summary?
After this, I put my position in writing and the principal gets a copy. That's all you're getting from me. Why did the zero go in before anyone called me?
